cards.explanation: The answer is long ago. The song says God's wonders are “…plans formed long ago…” Nothing was cooked up at the last minute here. My own plans usually get made while I'm standing in front of an open oven, friends, so this impresses me. (Isaiah 25:1)
The answer is False. The song says the fortress of strangers “…is a city no more; it will never be rebuilt.” That's final, friends. No rebuilding, no comeback tour. (Isaiah 25:2)

The answer is that they will honor Him. The song says, “Therefore, a strong people will honor You.” It goes on to say the cities of ruthless nations will revere Him. Strong people and ruthless nations both show up in that verse, bakers. (Isaiah 25:3)

The answer is the poor and the needy. The song says God has been “…a refuge for the poor, a stronghold for the needy in distress…” Those are the ones He covers, friends. I think that's a good thing to know about Him. (Isaiah 25:4)

The answer is silenced. The song says, “…so the song of the ruthless is silenced.” It's like a cloud sliding over the sun and cooling everything down. Quiet comes in, friends, and I'd take that over the noise any day. (Isaiah 25:5)
The answer is all the peoples. The LORD of Hosts will prepare a lavish banquet “…for all the peoples…” It's a wide-open table, friends. I like a guest list that big. (Isaiah 25:6)
The answer is death. Isaiah says, “He will swallow up death forever.” That comes right after the shroud and the sheet, friends. It's the biggest thing on that list, and it fits. (Isaiah 25:7-8)
The answer is False. Isaiah says, “He will swallow up death forever.” Not for a little while, friends, forever. Nothing temporary about it. (Isaiah 25:8)

The answer is tears. Isaiah says, “The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face…” Every face, bakers, not just a few. I think that's one of the most tender lines in this whole passage. (Isaiah 25:8)

The answer is waiting for Him. In that day they say, “we have waited for Him, and He has saved us.” They say it again: “This is the LORD for whom we have waited.” Waiting is what they talk about, friends, twice. (Isaiah 25:9)
The answer is trampled. Isaiah says, “…Moab will be trampled in his place…” The verse is blunt, friends, and it's heavy. (Isaiah 25:10)

The answer is his pride. Isaiah says, “His pride will be brought low, despite the skill of his hands.” Skilled hands didn't save it, friends. I've got a mustache that handles a whole cookie box, and I still try to stay humble about it. (Isaiah 25:11)

The answer is into the dust. Isaiah says, “The high-walled fortress will be brought down, cast to the ground, into the dust.” Tall walls, and they end up in the dust, friends. That's about as far down as it goes. (Isaiah 25:12)
